requirements.evidence: The contract is met: CreateQueue (app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:64) trims the name, slugifies `$slug ?? $name` and creates active queues; UpdateQueue takes nullable named params and its slug check uses `whereKeyNot($queue->id)` (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:253-318); SetQueueAccess upserts with `updateOrCreate`, deletes on an empty list and logs a revoke only when `$deleted > 0` (app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:180-201). It rejects cross-entity pairs and non-string or unknown permissions. QueuePolicy has create/update/manageAccess/call, and `is_array($permissions)` denies corrupted rows (app/Policies/QueuePolicy.php:531). CallNextTicket authorizes after the active check (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:32). Ticket::call locks the queue, then checks inactive, then authorizes, then checks waiting status (app/Models/Ticket.php:94-107). The migration has the unique pair and cascading FKs. No delete action was added. Gaps: the race-to-ValidationException fallback checks SQLSTATE '23000' or the case-sensitive substrings 'UNIQUE'/'Duplicate' (CreateQueue.php:115-125). That works for MySQL and SQLite but not for Postgres (SQLSTATE 23505, lowercase 'duplicate key'). It also treats any 23000 integrity error as a slug duplicate. Ticket::call locks the ticket before the queue, while CallNextTicket locks the queue first, so the two paths lock in opposite order.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes live in single-purpose actions that authorize inside the action through `Gate::forUser($actor)->authorize(...)`. Authorization is centralized in app/Policies/QueuePolicy.php (auto-discovered, checked in tests/Feature/QueuePolicyTest.php:1559). The model sets `#[Fillable([...])]` deliberately, matching sibling models (app/Models/QueueAccess.php:370). The migration has a generated-style timestamp name and a reversible `down()`. Audit events go to `Log::channel('audit')`. docs/business-rules.md, docs/database-schema.md and CHANGELOG.md 'Added' are updated. Public methods have PHPDoc. No service or repository layer was introduced.

security.evidence: Every write path authorizes first: CreateQueue.php:66, UpdateQueue.php:260, SetQueueAccess.php:165. Both call paths now enforce `call` (CallNextTicket.php:32, Ticket.php:107), replacing the weaker membership-only check. Employees cannot grant themselves access because manageAccess requires owner/admin. Cross-entity membership/queue pairs are rejected (SetQueueAccess.php:167). Permission entries are strictly checked with `is_string` and a strict `in_array`. Mass assignment is limited to the three intended columns. No weakness found.

tests.evidence: The tests are thorough. tests/Feature/QueueManagementTest.php covers create, slugify, owner/admin, invalid names, per-entity slug uniqueness, the denied matrix, independent updates, keeping its own slug, taking another queue's slug, and deactivation keeping tickets while failing issue/call. tests/Feature/QueueAccessTest.php covers schema, enum, casts and relations, factory same-entity behaviour, grant and revoke audit events, no log on a no-op revoke, invalid permissions, cross-entity pairs, non-manager denial including self-grant, and cascades. tests/Feature/QueuePolicyTest.php covers all abilities including a corrupted non-array value and Gate discovery. CallNextTicketTest checks unauthorized callers in every mode with no ticket change (line 910) and adds employee grant cases. IssueTicketTest checks inactive queues and auth before the already-called rule in Ticket::call. Existing tests were adapted to use an owner, not weakened. Missing: no test for the DB unique-index race path (QueryException -> ValidationException), and no test that an UpdateQueue with an invalid slug leaves the name unchanged.

simplicity.evidence: The code is mostly lean. However, `isUniqueViolation` and the slug pre-check plus `ValidationException::withMessages(['slug' => ...])` are copied verbatim between CreateQueue.php:101-125 and UpdateQueue.php:313-338. The QueueAccessFactory uses an `afterMaking` callback with nested branches (QueueAccessFactory.php:582-607) to keep both sides in the same entity. That is more involved than a definition using closures, but it works.

readability.evidence: Names are clear, methods are small, and comments explain the race handling (CreateQueue.php:89-90). The tests use named fixtures. There is minor noise: the long positional destructuring `[, $owner, , , $employeeMembership, $queue] = queueAccessFixture();` and an immediately-invoked closure inside one test (QueueAccessTest.php:1196-1202). The `$otherEntity` variables are unused in a few tests.

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task: actions, enum, model, factory, migration, policy, the two call-path changes, docs, changelog and tests. The CallNextTicketTest refactor to `callNextQueueWithOwner()` is required because the tests now need an authorized caller. No UI, delete action or extra permissions were added.

issues.explanation: The unique-violation detection relies on SQLSTATE '23000' or the case-sensitive substrings 'UNIQUE'/'Duplicate'. On Postgres (23505, 'duplicate key value') a race would surface as a raw QueryException, and any other 23000 integrity error would be reported as a slug duplicate.

Ticket::call locks the ticket row and then the queue row, while CallNextTicket locks the queue first and then tickets. Concurrent calls on the same queue can deadlock because the two paths take locks in opposite order.
Requirement 2 explicitly covers a DB unique-index race, but no test exercises the QueryException -> ValidationException path in CreateQueue or UpdateQueue.
`ensureSlugIsAvailable` and `isUniqueViolation` duplicate the CreateQueue code almost verbatim instead of sharing it.
Duplicate entries such as ['call', 'call'] are stored as-is; `array_values(array_unique(...))` would normalize the stored grant.
An immediately-invoked closure builds a fixture and leaves `$otherEntity` unused; several tests also destructure unused variables.

review.summary: The change adds CreateQueue, UpdateQueue and SetQueueAccess actions, a QueuePermission enum, the QueueAccess model, factory and migration, and a QueuePolicy that both call paths now enforce in the required order, with docs, changelog and extensive Pest tests. It follows the project conventions closely and has no security gaps. The remaining issues are minor: race detection is not portable across databases, Ticket::call and CallNextTicket lock in opposite order, the race path is untested and some helper code is duplicated, so I would approve with nits. Confidence is medium because a few helpers it relies on (`membershipFor`, UserRole, the audit channel) are not shown in the diff.
